outcome_semantics.ALLOWED: the value is rendered as is
outcome_semantics.REDACTED: removed on this surface; the recipient is entitled to it on another surface (typically in-app); no placeholder

resolution.match: row.recipient == recipient (no wildcard recipient) AND row.field in {field,'*'} AND row.channel in {channel,'*'} AND row.context in {context,'*'}
resolution.precedence: most specific row wins: field-exact first, then context-exact, then channel-exact (score = 4*field + 2*context + 1*channel); equal scores -> the more restrictive outcome
resolution.robustness: rows are generated so that the outcome is identical under context-first, channel-first and count-of-dimensions precedence (verified for every recipient x field x channel x context, including an unknown field); a W-D2 implementation of the charter chain therefore yields the same result
resolution.default: no matching row (unknown field, unknown recipient) -> PROHIBITED; an unknown recipient class is an error, never a permissive default

context_resolution.CASE_RESTRICTED: case.classification is RESTRICTED (or SECRET) AND the recipient's seat is NOT verified on the case's approved access list (DEC-F19 snapshot: active, cleared, conflict-free seats after Restricted Case Authority approval). Unknown or unverifiable membership -> CASE_RESTRICTED (fail closed). A recipient verified on the list is projected under '*' (or EXTERNAL when the delivery leaves the platform). The RESTRICTED_CASE_AUTHORITY of the case keeps its own rows.
context_resolution.EXTERNAL: the delivery is addressed outside CDF's organisational boundary: a mailbox outside the approved CDF domains (DEC-F22 governed external-email workflow), a letter or an export to an outside body. CDF corporate mailboxes of internal users are NOT external (context '*'). REFERRING_BODY deliveries are always EXTERNAL. For internal classes addressed externally the compact external profile applies (Q99 justification + classification check stay with the authority model, AUTHORIZE_NOTIFICATION).
context_resolution.CASE_PUBLIC: case.classification is PUBLIC; no row relaxes any field for this context (no source permits wider disclosure); resolution falls back to the '*' rows.
context_resolution.precedence_between_contexts: CASE_RESTRICTED takes precedence over EXTERNAL: a restricted case for a non-listed recipient is never sent anywhere

recipient_resolution: A seat holder recused, conflict-declared, excused for conflict or excluded by an upheld concern in the affected proceeding/meeting is RECUSED_MEMBER for every notice about it (overrides MEMBER/CHAIR).
DEPUTY_CHAIR with an acting-chair activation in force for the object (ADR-061 §5, DEC-F03) is CHAIR for that object; otherwise MEMBER.
ALTERNATE_SECRETARY and an active delegate of the secretary seat are SECRETARY (Q24; authz.is_committee_secretary).
The Grievance Committee's secretary, chair and members map to SECRETARY / CHAIR / MEMBER of that committee.
PLATFORM_ADMIN, DB_ADMIN, NOTIFICATION_ADMIN, SOC and audit roles are not recipient classes of case notifications (§21); oversight views show counts and states without content.
An unresolvable recipient is an error: project() must refuse, never fall back to a permissive class (D11-017 'unknown role: public only' is the floor).

eligibility_rules.rule: No notification is generated for a recipient not on a restricted case's approved access list; the CASE_RESTRICTED rows are the second line of defence.
No e-mail, SMS or card is generated for REPORTER while DEC-24 is OPEN; the portal is the only channel.
No notice is generated for REFERRING_BODY beyond the acknowledgement until D11-012 is decided (authority model SEND_REFERRAL_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT is SOURCE_REQUIRED).
A recipient whose access to the object ended receives no new notice about it; earlier notices keep no content (ADR-025).
Every renderer receives only a projected model (_disclosure_applied === true); anything else throws (charter §0.6).

per_surface_rule: One policy and one decision per field govern every surface of an experience. EMAIL experience = EMAIL_SUBJECT, EMAIL_PREHEADER, EMAIL_HTML, EMAIL_TEXT, CARD (+ the shared LINK, ATTACHMENT, METADATA, EXPORT, LOG); PLATFORM experience = IN_APP (+ the shared surfaces). Rows differ by channel only on the five e-mail surfaces, and identically on all five (twin parity MF-029; subject and preheader never wider than the body); the shared surfaces and IN_APP resolve to the '*' row, so an experience-level projection (most restrictive outcome across its surfaces, as the W-D2 projector computes) equals the e-mail row for e-mail and the '*' row for the platform. What each surface may CARRY of the projected fields is fixed by surface_composition (renderer contract enforced by REN/SEC tests); composition can only drop fields, never add one that the projection removed.

EMAIL_SUBJECT.rule: fixed event label + notice reference (or the safe reference); nothing else

EMAIL_PREHEADER.rule: repeats the event title only (preheader field PROHIBITED)

METADATA.rule: headers, card JSON properties, file names and idempotency keys carry the notice reference, template code and opaque ids only (recipient by opaque id, never an address, name or case number) while D11-024/D11-025 are OPEN

LOG.rule: logs carry ids, codes and states only (META keys: notification_id, type_code, recipient_ref, states); never names, addresses, case numbers, tokens or content

LINK.rule: URLs are ids-only paths (^(/[a-z0-9-]+)+$ for deep links); no query payload; a capability URL appears only in the subject's own message body and never in logs, metadata or exports

ATTACHMENT.rule: the .ics object carries title, logistics, notice reference and sender only; document attachments are PROHIBITED (field 'attachments')

EXPORT.rule: an export copy contains exactly the recipient's projection plus the record envelope (notification id, delivery and audit ids); capability URLs are replaced by their opaque id

meeting_info.en: Date, time, place, mode and online link of a meeting/hearing the recipient is invited to (also the .ics calendar object).
